_readme: WHICH REGISTRIES a box of this instance cannot pull from anonymously, and how bin/deploy.sh logs in to each.
KP-D1 (2026-10-21): the admin is pulled from the Forge release, whose images live in the product's PRIVATE
Artifact Registry. The customer's access is a READ-ONLY service account with NO KEY (the GCP organization
forbids service-account keys): the machine that deploys mints a 1-hour token by impersonating it
(gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=<it>), hands it to the box on ssh's STDIN for
`docker login`, and logs the box out after the pull. Nothing long-lived stays on the box or on disk here.
Nothing in this file is a secret: an e-mail names an account and grants nothing by itself. It is not in
deploy/<env>.env because a registry's door is the same for every environment of this instance, and those
files are the environment's. Read by bin/deploy.sh (step 3) through lock_gate_pull_logins (bin/lock-gate.sh).

southamerica-east1-docker.pkg.dev._private: forge-private-ok: functional — a GCP service account (a machine identity, not a person); bin/deploy.sh impersonates exactly this one
